symptom: mendixlabs/mxcli#1597 (case A): `@curve(from: (39, 0), to: (0, 61))` on a statement inside a `loop` or `while` body passed check and exec with no warning, and `describe` printed the body with no `@curve` — the same annotation after the loop was kept
cause: a loop body is built by its own flowBuilder; applyPendingAnnotations recorded the curve on that sub-builder's curveByOrigin, and addLoopStatement / addWhileStatement hoisted flows, annotationFlows, errors and the label registry to the parent but not the curves. applyFlowCurves runs once, on the builder that owns the flows, so the body's curves were never applied
file: mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_annotations.go (adoptCurves); cmd_microflows_builder_control.go (addLoopStatement, addWhileStatement); cmd_microflows_builder_flows.go (addErrorHandlerFlow now calls the same helper)
insight: #991 fixed exactly this for the error-handler builder a month earlier, at one of the three sites that hoist a sub-builder's flows — each site copies a hand-picked list of fields, so a fix at one is not a fix at the others. When a child builder's state is lost, grep `&flowBuilder{` for every sub-builder and diff the field lists their merge tails copy, rather than following the reported statement. The merge is now one helper (adoptCurves) the three sites share, and a nested loop test proves it chains through two levels. The main-line curve after the loop is the in-test control: it passed before the fix, so the test isolates the body
